incentives.name: Local property tax abatements (payment-in-lieu agreements)
incentives.what: Cities have offered data centers abatements, e.g., Little Rock and Conway each agreed to forgo 65% of property taxes for 30 years on $1B data center proposals; Clarksville weighed industrial development revenue bonds for Serverfarm.

incentives.name: Quick Action Closing Fund
incentives.what: State discretionary incentive fund for major projects (not data center specific); lawmakers in 2026 set aside up to $300M for a West Memphis 'superproject' that the budget labels 'advanced manufacturing, non-data center'.

dockets.what: Special rate contract for Google's West Memphis data center.
Certificate of environmental compatibility and public need for Cypress Solar (600 MW solar, 350 MW battery) serving the grid for Google's West Memphis data center.
Generating Arkansas Jobs Act rider update recovering costs of three generation projects including Cypress Solar from customers (added about $22.81 to one senator's bill).
Base rate case filed Feb 27, 2026 (data center provisions not confirmed in this sweep).

laws_and_bills.name: Generating Arkansas Jobs Act of 2025
laws_and_bills.what: Energy permitting and cost-recovery overhaul (lets utilities recover new generation costs through a rider during construction); credited with luring data centers.

laws_and_bills.name: Act 174 of 2024
laws_and_bills.what: Amended the law on digital asset mining (crypto 'data centers') and banned ownership by foreign-party-controlled interests from listed adversary countries; enforcement against Jones Eagle temporarily blocked by a federal court (Nov 2024).

laws_and_bills.name: Act 851 of 2023
laws_and_bills.what: Bars local governments from banning data centers (the crypto-mining 'data center' law); Talk Business notes it does not bar local rules that cause delays or significant restrictions.

local_rules.what: Five-year moratorium on data centers, passed unanimously by the quorum court.

Regulations for data centers in unincorporated areas: electrical load analyses, water and wastewater plans, land-use studies, decommissioning plans, proof utilities won't be impaired. Passed 11-4; vetoed by County Judge Barry Hyde; override expected to be sought. An earlier moratorium vote in June was voided over a miscount.

Requirements for data centers of 250,000+ sq ft using over 50 MW, including a report on total daily water use before approval (Mayor Frank Scott's framework); Advocate says Little Rock passed its requirements over the summer.

At an Aug 11, 2026 study session, city directors asked staff to draft rules to discourage data centers: a zoning code amendment (utility capacity certifications, water use reports, larger setbacks, noise limits), board approval for water connections 2 inches or larger, and a data center water rate class at four times current rates. No known data center is being considered in the Fort Smith metro.
Talk Business reports Fayetteville has adopted stricter data center rules (details not checked).
